Senses.Explanation: Ten generations, past and present, never leave this present thought. The couplet enters the Chan hall as inherited authority — most windows lift it with a so-it-is-said or a have-you-not-heard — and the masters spend it on the one thought everyone is using right now. Ruibai Mingxue, closing the retreat over tea, sets it first and then unpacks the present-thought: leaving home is this one thought, wandering is this one thought, seeking good teachers is this one thought, entering the retreat-hall is this one thought, biting teeth and glaring, raising fists and arms, scrubbing and straining, researching truth and cutting doubt — every doing of yours never leaves this one thought. Do you all recognize this one thought? Yuan'an Liao lets the spring carry it: within the patched-robe's inner chamber there is the machinery of heaven-and-earth's trimming, and between the worker's bellows the freedom of gathering and releasing — a search of cold trees, three light wrappings, morning play in Tantra's clouds, evening lodging on Luofu's moon, then one knows the borderless realm does not separate self and other by a hair-tip; and besides — a few plum trees, half a bank of willows, mist scattering the scenery before the kalpa, fragrance streaming in a spring beyond things — all without leaving the present thought; so the twelve hours need not turn: a short lifespan can be stretched into long years, the Southern Basket moved to be the Northern Dipper. Xiuye Minglin gathers a thousand sages into one hall that receives no mote of dust, melts past-and-present into one quarter-hour — most marvelous, most divine — and if you believe it, you save strength: ten generations, past and present, never leave this present thought; and not only the twelve hours: push the sexagenary cycle backwards and you can turn the year's head into its tail, strike the third watch at high noon, stretch one thought into three asankhyeya kalpas without lengthening, squeeze the three kalpas into one thought without shortening. Lianyue Daozheng raises the Platform Sutra on moving the Western Land east — and grades the Great Master's words: direct and quick as the lifting is, to see the West it is still a hundred and eight thousand off; have you not heard — the borderless kalpa-ocean does not separate self and other by a hair-tip; ten generations, past and present, never leave this present thought — seen thus, one eye level: what east? what west? what pure? what defiled? Lanshi Ling seals his retirement with it: at midnight the wooden man comes pulling on his boots, at daybreak the stone woman goes off wearing her hat; staying, the seal goes; going, the seal stays; coming and going without appearance, the two sides sealing without mind — and today's report known, the old monk unties his waist-bundle, cooks rice without rice, boils soup of wooden twigs, and winters with the brothers. And Tian'an Sheng turns on the pair of formulas themselves: stirring the long river into curd, changing the great earth into gold — a hayseed's family plate; the borderless realm not separated by a hair-tip — the talk chopped into two stumps; ten generations never leaving the present thought — legs drawn on the snake.
